mira: Heads up — seeing ~40 pods stuck Pending in us-west1b since 09:02. They all request 1gpu but the scheduler keeps scattering them; lots of tiny slots left unused. Anyone else? :eyes:
sam: Yup, noticed. kube-scheduler logs show repeated 'No nodes available that match pod's node affinity/taints' even though nodes show free GPU capacity. smells like fractional gang packing + strict affinity mismatch.
jordan: Quick check: some nodes have taint `gpu.reserved=true:NoSchedule` (warm-pool) and these jobs don't have the toleration. Also seeing NIC egress saturating on rack r3 -> some nodes temporarily reporting high tx drops.
mira: kubectl describe of one stuck pod (truncated):
```
Name: test-job-7k9p
Node-Selectors: accelerator=rtx6000
Tolerations: <none>
Events:
  09:02:01  FailedScheduling  0/24 nodes are available: 3 node(s) had taint {gpu.reserved=true:NoSchedule}, 10 node(s) didn't match pod affinity/selector.
```
devon: infra-bot: ALERT us-west1b gpu-pool low-allocable - 12% allocable GPUs; 3 nodes marked NotReady (kernel OOM) in last 15m.
sam: That explains the mismatch. Scheduler's binpack topology plugin is over-sharding tiny requests across racks; combined with warm-pool taints we get stranded small free GPUs. Short-term fixes: 1) add toleration for warm-pool taint to the low-priority queue, 2) relax topologySpread for tiny-gang jobs, 3) enable 10m coalescing window so scheduler can batch small requests.
jordan: Agree. Long term we should adjust packing policy to prefer filling warm-pool nodes first for preemptible workloads, and add a small backfill allowance to avoid leaving 1GPU holes. Cost note: allowing warm-pool tolerations may increase reserved utilization by ~0.4% (estimate) but should cut SLO violations by ~5%.
mira: I'll do a quick canary: annotate the low-priority queue pods with toleration for `gpu.reserved=true` and toggle topologySpread to 'prefer' instead of 'require' for that queue. Rolling to 10 pods in us-west1b first. Plan posted to incident thread.
devon: TY — can you paste the exact rollout + rollback commands? I'll create the incident runbook entry and tag oncall.
sam: Also capturing metric: eviction_rate_us-west1b spiked to 18/min during the window, correlates with the churn when nodes went NotReady. If the canary doesn't help, we should temporarily disable strict topology for that node pool.
mira: OK creating the rollout now (kubectl patch jobqueue ...). Will update with outcome in ~5m.
